Internal employee knowledge-transfer guide

Findoly CRM Employee Guide

A practical guide to daily lead operations, provider management, communication, billing, reporting and administration.

Production UI referenceScreenshot set: 7 August 2026Version 1.1
Internal use only. Screenshots have been cropped and masked to protect customer, provider, employee and financial information. Do not forward this guide outside authorised Findoly teams.
How to use this guide

Start here

Use this guide during onboarding, refresher training and day-to-day operations. Your role may show fewer menus or actions than the administrator screenshots. Always follow the permissions and approval process assigned to you.

1. Locate the moduleUse the sidebar or the contents menu in this guide.
2. Follow the standard workflowComplete the steps in order and verify the final record state.
3. Escalate safelyShare record IDs, timestamps and safe error codes - never OTPs, passwords or API credentials.

Recommended daily routine

  1. Log in and confirm your displayed role.
  2. Review Dashboard totals and recent requirements.
  3. Process assigned requirements and provider requests.
  4. Review open Follow-ups.
  5. Check WhatsApp Inbox unread conversations.
  6. Review failed communication logs when part of your role.
  7. Before ending the shift, update statuses and leave clear follow-up ownership.

Core operating principles

  • Search before creating a new record.
  • Verify identity before changing contact or payment data.
  • Use the least privilege required for the task.
  • Never share OTPs, tokens or credentials.
  • Do not make financial commitments without authority.
  • Keep customer communication factual and professional.
  • Use record IDs and timestamps for technical escalation.
  • Do not export or download data without a work need.

Status language used in the CRM

StatusOperational meaning
Active / DeactivatedWhether the record or access is currently enabled. Always check the underlying record before advising a user.
PendingAn action or outcome still requires processing or confirmation.
Approved / RejectedA review decision has been recorded. Check who acted and why before changing it.
Open / ClosedThe work item or conversation still requires attention, or has been completed for now.
Accepted / Sent / Delivered / ReadCommunication delivery stages. Accepted does not necessarily mean delivered.
FailedThe action did not complete. Review the safe error details and avoid repeated attempts without diagnosis.
Scope: The screenshots primarily show overview and list pages. Create/edit forms and exact permissions may vary by role and later releases. This guide explains what the supplied production screenshots support and does not invent hidden fields.
Access and security

1. Login and OTP verification

Use the login flow to access the CRM with the mobile number registered against your employee account. The second screen verifies the one-time password (OTP).

Use this feature when

  • At the start of a work session
  • After the session expires or you sign out
  • When an administrator asks you to verify access after a role or status change

Employee objective

Complete the required action accurately, leave the record in a clear state, and preserve enough context for the next employee or manager.

Main controls

Mobile numberEnter the mobile number assigned to your CRM employee profile.
Send / Request OTPRequests a one-time password through the configured authentication channel.
OTP fieldsEnter the received code exactly as delivered.
Verify / Sign inCompletes authentication and opens the CRM if the account is active and authorised.

Standard workflow

  1. Open the official CRM address supplied by Findoly.
  2. Enter only your registered employee mobile number.
  3. Request the OTP and wait for the current code.
  4. Enter the OTP once; do not repeatedly request codes unless the first request has clearly expired.
  5. After login, confirm that your name and role shown in the top-right account area are correct.

Quality and safety checks

  • Never share an OTP in chat, email, screenshots or support tickets.
  • Do not use another employee’s account, even temporarily.
  • If your role, name or available menu items look incorrect, stop and contact an administrator before changing records.
Guide note: The screenshots have been masked so the registered mobile number and OTP are not visible.
Daily starting point

2. Dashboard

The Dashboard provides a quick operational view of requirements, providers, marketplace activity and follow-ups. It is the recommended first page after login.

Use this feature when

  • At the beginning of each shift
  • Before assigning work or following up
  • When management needs a quick view of current operational volume

Employee objective

Complete the required action accurately, leave the record in a clear state, and preserve enough context for the next employee or manager.

Main controls

Summary cardsShow headline totals such as all requirements, active providers, available offers and open follow-ups.
Recent requirementsShows the latest customer requirements and their current status.
OpenOpens a requirement for detailed review.
Quick actionsProvides shortcuts to create a requirement, add a provider, review provider unlocks or open reports.
Global searchSearches leads, customers or mobile numbers from the header.

Standard workflow

  1. Review the summary cards for unexpected changes or backlogs.
  2. Check Recent requirements for new or pending work.
  3. Open records that need verification, pricing or status updates.
  4. Review Open follow-ups so customer or provider commitments are not missed.
  5. Use Quick actions only when you are ready to complete the corresponding workflow.

Quality and safety checks

  • Dashboard totals are indicators; open the underlying list before making a decision.
  • Do not treat “available offers” as confirmed customer outcomes.
  • Escalate unusual spikes, missing counts or records that cannot be opened.
Guide note: The recent-requirements rows are blurred in this guide to protect production customer information.
Lead management

3. Requirements

Requirements are customer service needs recorded in the CRM. This page is used to find, verify, price and distribute customer requirements according to the approved operating process.

Use this feature when

  • A new customer requirement must be created
  • An existing lead must be verified or updated
  • You need to find a requirement by customer, mobile, title, lead ID or referral ID
  • You need to review requirements by status, category, source or date

Employee objective

Complete the required action accurately, leave the record in a clear state, and preserve enough context for the next employee or manager.

Main controls

Create leadStarts a new requirement record.
SearchFinds records by customer, mobile, title or lead ID.
FiltersExpands status, record state, category, source, referral ID, validation state and date controls.
Date field / rangeFilters using the selected date type and from/to dates.
Sort by dateChanges the order of results.
RowsControls how many records appear on the current page.
ClearResets applied search and filter values.

Standard workflow

  1. Search for the customer first to avoid creating a duplicate requirement.
  2. Open the relevant record and verify customer, category, location and requirement details.
  3. Use the validation and status fields according to your role and operating policy.
  4. Confirm pricing and marketplace details before approval or distribution.
  5. Add or update follow-up information when the customer or provider requires a later action.
  6. Re-check the record after saving to confirm the intended status is visible.

Quality and safety checks

  • Do not create duplicate leads for the same request merely because a search filter is active.
  • Do not approve or publish incomplete, test or unverified customer data in production.
  • Do not enter emojis, HTML or unsupported special content in fields that require plain text.
  • Use referral IDs carefully; they may be used for partner attribution and reporting.
Guide note: The visible page supports broad filtering. Apply only the filters needed, then clear them before concluding that a record is missing.
Provider network

4. Providers

The Providers directory is used to manage service partners, their eligibility, categories, service area, portal access and credit visibility.

Use this feature when

  • Onboarding a new service provider
  • Reviewing provider access or status
  • Checking provider categories, area or credit balance
  • Finding a provider by name, business, mobile or identifier

Employee objective

Complete the required action accurately, leave the record in a clear state, and preserve enough context for the next employee or manager.

Main controls

New providerStarts provider creation.
Search providerFinds a provider by provider name, business, mobile or other visible identifier.
StatusFilters all, active or other provider states available to your role.
Date / From / ToFilters the directory by the selected date field and date range.
SortOrders provider records.
ViewOpens provider details.
EditOpens permitted provider fields for update.

Standard workflow

  1. Search existing providers before adding a new account.
  2. Open the provider and verify contact, category and service area information.
  3. Confirm portal access and active status before advising the provider to log in.
  4. Review credits only for operational support; financial adjustments must follow authorised procedures.
  5. After edits, confirm the directory reflects the correct status and access state.

Quality and safety checks

  • A CRM employee, agent or provider may legitimately share an identity where the approved system allows it; do not create duplicate records to bypass validation.

  • Do not manually promise credits or subscription benefits without authorisation.

Onboarding review

5. Provider requests

Provider requests contain applications or onboarding requests that require review before becoming fully usable provider accounts.

Use this feature when

  • A new provider application arrives
  • A rejected request needs a later status review
  • You need to filter requests by status, category, date or other available criteria

Employee objective

Complete the required action accurately, leave the record in a clear state, and preserve enough context for the next employee or manager.

Main controls

View provider requestsOpens or refreshes the request list.
Search and filtersNarrow the list using the visible request criteria.
Status tabs / filtersSeparate pending, approved, rejected or other request states available in the page.
View / action controlsOpen the request and perform only actions permitted by your role.

Standard workflow

  1. Open the oldest relevant pending request first unless management has set another priority.
  2. Verify contact details, service category, service area and submitted information.
  3. Check whether the same contact already exists as an employee, agent, provider or earlier request.
  4. Approve, reject or retain the request in its current state based on evidence and policy.
  5. Record a clear reason when a decision or status change requires explanation.

Quality and safety checks

  • Do not reject only because the same mobile number belongs to an employee or agent when the approved CRM rules permit multiple roles.
  • Do not approve incomplete or unverifiable provider information.
  • Use status changes rather than deleting history unless an authorised deletion process specifically applies.
Guide note: Request rows are masked; headings and controls remain visible.

Finance operations

7. Partner payouts / withdrawals

This page tracks partner withdrawal or payout requests and their processing status.

Use this feature when

  • A partner has submitted a withdrawal request
  • Finance needs to review pending or completed requests
  • You need to locate a transaction by partner, status or date

Employee objective

Complete the required action accurately, leave the record in a clear state, and preserve enough context for the next employee or manager.

Main controls

Search and filtersNarrows requests using the criteria available on the page.
StatusSeparates pending, approved, rejected, paid or other configured states.
Date range / sortLocates requests for a specific accounting period.
RowsChanges page size.

Standard workflow

  1. Verify the partner identity and the exact request being processed.
  2. Check amount, payout method and current status.
  3. Confirm the request has not already been paid or rejected.
  4. Perform only the action authorised for your finance role.

Quality and safety checks

  • Do not change bank or UPI details during payout processing without an authorised identity-verification process.
  • Escalate duplicate, suspicious or mismatched requests immediately.
Guide note: Financial records are masked. This guide does not replace finance approval policy.
Catalog management

8. Categories

Categories define the top-level service catalog used by customer requirements and provider eligibility.

Use this feature when

  • A new service category is approved
  • An existing category needs a controlled update
  • You need to review category coverage or status

Employee objective

Complete the required action accurately, leave the record in a clear state, and preserve enough context for the next employee or manager.

Main controls

Manage categoriesOpens category management.
Create categoryAdds a new top-level service category.
Search / filtersFinds category records.
Edit / status actionsChange supported category information when permitted.

Standard workflow

  1. Search for the proposed category name and slug before creating it.
  2. Use a clear customer-facing name that matches the approved service taxonomy.
  3. Set status and any required display or operational fields carefully.
  4. Save and verify how the category appears in the list.
  5. Coordinate with subcategory management so providers and requirement forms remain consistent.

Quality and safety checks

  • Do not create near-duplicate categories with different spelling.
  • Do not rename a live category without understanding effects on provider matching, forms, reporting and automation rules.
  • Do not deactivate a category that still has active operational use without management approval.
Guide note: Catalog changes can affect multiple workflows. Treat them as controlled configuration, not routine text edits.

10. Provider unlocks

Provider unlocks show provider-specific lead access records. Marketplace visibility by itself does not create a provider unlock row.

Use this feature when

  • Confirming that a provider accessed a requirement
  • Reviewing the access method, credit cost or outcome
  • Investigating a provider’s lead-access complaint

Employee objective

Complete the required action accurately, leave the record in a clear state, and preserve enough context for the next employee or manager.

Main controls

Lead reference IDFilters by the requirement/lead identifier.
Provider IDFilters by the provider identifier.
MethodFilters by access method, such as credits or another configured method.
OutcomeFilters by pending, confirmed or other recorded results.
Date range / sortFinds unlocks within a period.
Apply / ClearRuns or resets filters.

Standard workflow

  1. Search with the lead reference ID or provider ID when investigating a specific case.
  2. Verify the provider, category, method, credits and unlock time.
  3. Review the outcome and any related follow-up before giving a provider an answer.
  4. Use the underlying requirement and provider records for additional context.
  5. Escalate credit or payment inconsistencies with both record IDs and timestamps.

Quality and safety checks

  • Do not interpret marketplace visibility as proof that a provider accessed customer details.
  • Do not manually recreate unlock records to fix a complaint.
  • Do not alter credits without the authorised wallet/finance workflow.

Operations

11. Follow-ups

Follow-ups track actions that must happen later, helping employees avoid missed customer, provider or operational commitments.

Use this feature when

  • A customer asks to be contacted later
  • A provider or partner requires a scheduled response
  • An enquiry, payout or onboarding item needs another review

Employee objective

Complete the required action accurately, leave the record in a clear state, and preserve enough context for the next employee or manager.

Main controls

New follow-upCreates a scheduled follow-up.
Search and filtersFinds follow-ups by visible status, owner, date or related record criteria.
Open / completed statusSeparates outstanding work from completed items.
Rows / sortControls list size and ordering.

Standard workflow

  1. Create the follow-up from the relevant record when possible so the relationship is preserved.
  2. Set a realistic due date and clear purpose.
  3. Review open follow-ups at the start and end of the shift.
  4. Complete the action, add the outcome if supported, then mark it complete.
  5. Re-schedule only with a genuine reason; do not keep overdue items open without explanation.

Quality and safety checks

  • A follow-up is not a substitute for updating the underlying requirement or provider status.
  • Do not store sensitive customer details in unnecessary free text.
  • Escalate overdue high-priority items to the responsible manager.
Guide note: The screenshot shows the empty/list state and filtering area.
Customer and operational messaging

12. Communication Center

The Communication Center separates WhatsApp and email management into focused pages. It also provides internal Amazon SES email alerts, OTP activity, templates, automations and delivery logs.

Use this feature when

  • Sending an approved manual message
  • Managing reusable templates
  • Connecting events to communication rules
  • Checking whether a message was accepted, delivered or failed
  • Reviewing channel configuration health

Employee objective

Complete the required action accurately, leave the record in a clear state, and preserve enough context for the next employee or manager.

Main controls

WhatsAppManages approved Gupshup templates, WhatsApp automations and WhatsApp delivery logs.
EmailManages Amazon SES templates, email automations, internal alerts and email delivery logs.
Internal alertsControls operational emails sent to alert@findoly.com for new leads, Partners and Providers.
OTP activityReviews recent OTP activity and delivery outcomes.
Search logsFinds recent WhatsApp or email communication by identifier, event and status.

Standard workflow

  1. Choose the correct channel and approved template.
  2. Confirm the recipient and related record before sending.
  3. Use automation rules only when the event, audience and template are fully understood.
  4. After sending, check Message logs for provider acceptance and later delivery status.
  5. Investigate failed messages using the communication ID, channel and safe error details.

Quality and safety checks

  • Communication and OTP activity logs shown here are automatically deleted after 7 days, as stated on the page.
  • Do not expose API keys, webhook tokens or complete customer data in support logs.
  • Template changes may require external WhatsApp approval; a CRM save does not guarantee immediate availability.
  • Do not use bulk or automated messaging without approved audience and content.
Guide note: Use the Communication Center for templates, rules and delivery history. Use WhatsApp Inbox for ongoing two-way customer conversations.
Shared customer inbox

13. WhatsApp Inbox

The WhatsApp Inbox is the shared workspace for customers who directly message the Findoly WhatsApp number. Conversations are grouped by customer number and can be managed by authorised CRM employees.

Use this feature when

  • A customer sends a WhatsApp message
  • A customer provides more information or media
  • An employee needs to reply during the available service window
  • A conversation must be marked unread, closed or reopened

Employee objective

Complete the required action accurately, leave the record in a clear state, and preserve enough context for the next employee or manager.

Main controls

Conversation listShows customer conversations and unread activity.
Search name or mobileFinds a conversation.
Open / closed filterLimits the conversation state.
Unread onlyShows conversations still requiring review.
RefreshRequests the latest conversation list.
Message paneDisplays the selected conversation history.
Reply composerSends a session reply through the configured WhatsApp provider.
View message logsOpens delivery history and technical status.

Standard workflow

  1. Open Communication Center → WhatsApp Inbox.
  2. Prioritise unread and open conversations.
  3. Select a customer and read the entire recent thread before replying.
  4. Check linked requirement information where available.
  5. For a shared location, review the displayed name, address and coordinates, then use Open in Google Maps when operationally required.
  6. Write a clear, short and professional response.
  7. Send once, then confirm the message appears in the thread and progresses through the available delivery statuses.
  8. Close the conversation only when no further operational action is pending.

Quality and safety checks

  • A customer message opens or refreshes the WhatsApp customer-service window; outside the permitted window, an approved template may be required.
  • Do not promise price, refund, provider availability or resolution without verified authority.
  • Customer images, documents, audio, video and shared locations are operational data; open or download them only for legitimate work.
  • Confirm the exact service location with the customer when access, building entry or site conditions matter.
  • Do not copy or share customer coordinates outside the approved operational process.
  • Do not move customer files to personal storage.
  • Provider “View Enquiry” action messages are not normal customer conversations.
Guide note: The screenshot shows the empty state. In an active conversation, the left side contains conversations and the right side contains message history, media previews, location cards and reply controls.
Communication audit

14. Message logs

Message logs provide channel-specific delivery and processing history for WhatsApp and email; OTP activity remains separate.

Use this feature when

  • A customer says a message was not received
  • A sent message shows failed or pending
  • You need to confirm template, channel, recipient type or provider status
  • Technical support requests a communication ID or timestamp

Employee objective

Complete the required action accurately, leave the record in a clear state, and preserve enough context for the next employee or manager.

Main controls

SearchFinds logs using the available identifiers or text.
ChannelUse the dedicated WhatsApp or Email log page; OTP activity remains a separate page.
StatusFilters accepted, sent, delivered, read, failed or other states.
Date / related filtersNarrows the audit history.
View detailsOpens the safe metadata available for the communication.

Standard workflow

  1. Search using the communication ID, related record or a narrow date window.
  2. Confirm the channel and direction.
  3. Read the chronological status: queued/accepted, sent, delivered, read or failed.
  4. For failure, capture the safe error code and request/communication ID.
  5. Retry only through the supported workflow; do not resend repeatedly without checking the first attempt.

Quality and safety checks

  • Accepted means the provider accepted the request, not necessarily that the customer received it.
  • Delivered and read depend on provider callbacks and recipient/device behaviour.
  • Do not paste full mobile numbers, message content, tokens or personal data into technical tickets.
Guide note: Communication history is masked in the guide.

  3. Separate view, send, edit, approve, delete and finance permissions where the CRM provides them.
  4. Save and test with a non-production or controlled employee account.
  5. Document management approval for privileged access.
  6. Review and remove access when responsibilities change.

Quality and safety checks

  • Avoid broad catch-all roles.
  • Do not give billing, payout, employee or role-management permission to general operational users.
  • Test both allowed and denied actions; seeing a menu is not the only access check.
Guide note: Role names are visible because they describe internal access design; permission changes should remain restricted to authorised administrators.
